chunks: From him, from Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) who said:

Patience and satisfaction from Allah are the head of the obedience of Allah, and whoever is patient and satisfied from Allah regarding what He has decreed for him, whether he loves it or dislikes it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will decree for him regarding what he loves or dislikes, except what is better for him.

key_terms.الصَّبْرُ: Patience, perseverance in the face of hardship

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of patience and satisfaction with divine decree in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In Shia theology, this hadith from al-Kafi elevates rida (satisfaction) beyond mere endurance to an active spiritual state that aligns the believer's will with divine wisdom, serving as the foundation of true ta'ah (obedience). It assures that such inner contentment guarantees the efficacy of divine decree, ensuring that all outcomes—whether perceived as pleasant or painful—are ultimately beneficial. This concept is central to the Shia understanding of theodicy, linking personal spiritual maturity with trust in God's perfect justice.
